extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners, and patent examiners (plant patents/drawings)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards for preparing and submitting drawings (including photographs and color renderings) in plant patent applications, covering format, paper, sizing, margins, labeling, numbering, and grounds for objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistically and competently executed
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant patent drawings should be artistically and competently executed and must comply with the requirements of § 1.84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View numbers and reference characters need not be employed unless required by the examiner. The drawing must disclose all the distinctive characteristics of the plant capable of visual representation. Form paragraph ¶ 16.07 may be used to object under 37 CFR 1.165(a) where a figure is not artistically and/or competently executed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings when color is distinguishing
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawings may be in color. The drawing must be in color if color is a distinguishing characteristic of the new variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two copies of color drawings or photographs must be submitted. If drawings, including watercolor renderings or photographs, are in color, two color copies of each drawing or photograph are required. If the required copies of the drawings are not included, the application will be accorded a filing date, but correction will be required before the application is forwarded for examination. Form paragraph ¶ 16.06: 'Color Drawings Must Be in Duplicate' (objection under 37 CFR 1.165(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with drawing standards (§ 1.84)
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings submitted must meet the Standards for drawings set out in 37 CFR 1.84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: § 1.84 contains multiple specific subrequirements (identification, paper type, sheet size, margins, arrangement of views, numbering, etc.) which must all be satisfied. See separate criteria below for those specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of drawings (title, inventor, application/docket number)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia should be provided and, if provided, should include the title of the invention, inventor’s name, and application number, or docket number (if any).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If this information is provided, it must be placed on the front of each sheet within the top margin. Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date must be identified as either 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' pursuant to § 1.121(d). Marked-up copies of amended drawing figures with annotations must be clearly labeled as 'Annotated Sheet' pursuant to § 1.121(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be made on paper which is flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny, and durable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All sheets must be reasonably free from cracks, creases, and folds. Only one side of the sheet may be used for the drawing. Each sheet must be reasonably free from erasures and must be free from alterations, overwritings, and interlineations. Photographs must be developed on paper meeting the sheet-size and margin requirements of the regulations; see paragraph (b) for other requirements for photographs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size of paper
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawing sheets in an application must be the same size; allowed sizes are 21.0 cm by 29.7 cm (DIN A4) or 21.6 cm by 27.9 cm (8 1/2 by 11 inches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the shorter sides of the sheet is regarded as its top.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins and sight dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets must not contain frames around the sight but should have scan target points (cross-hairs) printed on two cater-corner margin corners; specified margins create the 'sight' area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each sheet must include a top margin of at least 2.5 cm (1 inch), a left margin of at least 2.5 cm (1 inch), a right margin of at least 1.5 cm (5/8 inch), and a bottom margin of at least 1.0 cm (3/8 inch). These margins leave a sight no greater than 17.0 cm by 26.2 cm on A4 sheets and no greater than 17.6 cm by 24.4 cm on 8 1/2 by 11 inch sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of views
rubrics_metrics.description: One view must not be placed upon another or within the outline of another; all views on the same sheet should stand in the same direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If possible, views should be readable with the sheet held in an upright position. If views wider than the sheet are necessary, the sheet may be turned on its side so the top (with heading space) is on the right-hand side. Words must appear horizontal left-to-right when the page is upright or turned so top becomes right side, except for graphs following standard scientific axis conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of sheets of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets of drawings should be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals, starting with 1, within the sight as defined by margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These numbers, if present, must be placed in the middle of the top of the sheet (but not in the margin). Numbers can be placed on the right-hand side if the drawing extends too close to the middle. Drawing sheet numbering must be clear and larger than numbers used as reference characters. The number of each sheet should be shown by two Arabic numerals placed on either side of an oblique line (first = sheet number; second = total number of sheets), with no other marking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of views (FIG. numbering)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different views must be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals, starting with 1, independent of sheet numbering; view numbers should be preceded by the abbreviation 'FIG.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial views intended to form one complete view on one or several sheets must be identified by the same number followed by a capital letter. View numbers and letters must be simple and clear (no brackets, circles, inverted commas) and must be larger than reference character numbers. Where only a single view is used, it must not be numbered and 'FIG.' must not appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: No holes in drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: No holes should be made by applicant in the drawing sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph ¶ 16.11 (Drawing Figures Not Competently Executed) and other drawing objections may be used where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs and watercolor renderings requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs and watercolor renderings used as drawings must follow color-copy and paper requirements and must disclose distinguishing characteristics capable of visual representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If photographs or watercolor renderings are in color, two color copies of each are required. Photographs must be developed on paper meeting the sheet-size and margin requirements; only one side of the sheet may be used for the drawing. Failure to supply required copies may result in an objection and required correction prior to examination forwarding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for drawing objections (form paragraphs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard form paragraphs identify common drawing defects that can be objected to under 37 CFR 1.165.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: ¶ 16.06 'Color Drawings Must Be in Duplicate' (objection under 37 CFR 1.165(b)); ¶ 16.07 'Drawing Figures Not Competently Executed' (objection under 37 CFR 1.165(a)); ¶ 16.11 'Drawings in Improper Scale' (objection under 37 CFR 1.165(a)) — e.g., drawings inadequate in scale to show distinguishing features of the plant.
